subject: Covariance between exogenous and endogenous latent variables in SEM

messages.author: 999e6e262ffc2d33
messages.subject: Covariance between exogenous and endogenous latent variables in SEM
parts:
Hello,

I have a question about correlated latent exogenous and latent endogenous variables.

Long story short i am wondering is stipulating a covariance relation betwean an endogenous latent variable (therefore its residual part) and an exogenous latent variable allowed.


Explanation:

I am running an extended Theory of planned behavior model of digital piracy. The original model has 3 exogenous latent variables (attitude, subjective norms and perceived behavioral control) and 1 endogenous latent variable (intention).

When i run the original model with the syntax bellow, my model has a good fit. When i run the original model lavaan output gives me an account of covariance between my exogenous variables ATT and SN, ATT and PBC SN and PBC.


model1 <- 'ATT  =~ att1 + att2 + att3 + att4 + att6 + att7
SN =~ sn1 + sn2 + sn3r + sn5r
PBC =~ pbc1 + pbc2 + pbc4 + pbc5
INT =~ int1 + int3 + int4 + int5

INT ~ ATT + SN + PBC'

The model looks like this: https://www.comminit.com/files/tpb.jpg

 

The extended TPB adds two latent variables PUNISHMENT CERTAINTY and PUSNIHMENT SEVERITY that impact the ATTITUDE variable making it a de facto endogenous variable . The syntax is bellow.


model2 <- 'ATT  =~ att1 + att2 + att3 + att4 + att6 + att7

SN =~ sn1 + sn2 + sn3r + sn5r

PBC =~ pbc1 + pbc2 + pbc4 + pbc5
INT =~ int1 + int3 + int4 + int5
CERTAINTY =~ cert3 + cert4 + cert2
SEVERITY =~ ps2 + ps3 + ps1r
INT ~ ATT + SN + PBC
ATT ~ CERTAINTY + SEVERITY '


When i run this model i no longer get the covariance between the ATT and SN and ATT and PBC. The covariances that the output shows me are: CERTAINTY ~~ SEVERITY, CERTAINTY ~~ PBC, CERTAINTY ~~ SN, SEVERITY ~~ PBC, SEVERITY~~SN.


However, the variables ATT, SN and PBC are heavily correlated in my data and i suspect that the fact that the correlations between ATT and SN and PBC are not included in the model (because ATTITUDE became an endogenous latent variable) severely worsens my model fit.


For example, my model implies that the influence sign of the SEVERITY on ATTITUDE is not what the theory predicts. It implies that for every one unit of reduction in PUNISHMENT SEVERITY the respondents ATTITUDES toward piracy worsen.  Also my standardised residual matrix shows severe model misfit.

 

I tried testing the following model and the signs in the regressions are what the theory would expect.


model3 <- 'ATT  =~ att1 + att2 + att3 + att4 + att6 + att7
CERTAINTY =~ cert3 + cert4 + cert2
SEVERITY =~ ps2 + ps3 + ps1r
ATT ~ CERTAINTY + SEVERITY'

 

 I tried searching on the internet and among other papers that used lavaan and the extended TPB and i saw that there are models where the ATITUTE is an endogenous variable but the authors included covariance relations between ATT and SN and PBC in the model syntax.

 

Given that i am a beginner in SEM i am wondering is stipulating such a covariance between ATITUDE (even if it is endogenous) PBC and SN (exogenous) allowed.

 

If i include ATT ~~ PBC + SN in my model, my model fit is greatly improved.

When i run the following syntax:

model4<- 'ATT  =~ att1 + att2 + att3 + att4 + att6 + att7

SN =~ sn1 + sn2 + sn3r + sn5r

PBC =~ pbc1 + pbc2 + pbc4 + pbc5
INT =~ int1 + int3 + int4 + int5


CERTAINTY =~ cert3 + cert4 + cert2
SEVERITY =~ ps2 + ps3 + ps1r


INT ~ ATT + SN + PBC
ATT ~ CERTAINTY + SEVERITY

ATT ~~ PBC + SN '

 

in the covariances section of the output lavaan shows me the covariance between .ATT ~~ PBC and , .ATT~~SN. In other words, i get a covariance between the residual part of ATTITUDE and PBC and SN. I understand why this is i am just interested is this final model syntax allowed.

 

Sorry if i am not making sense in some parts of my question.

 

Thanks so much in advance for your answers.


Miljan

messages.author: 08e48595b188026f
messages.subject: Re: Covariance between exogenous and endogenous latent variables in SEM
parts:
Hi Miljan,

I'd say that (a) it is statistically allowed and (b) it is allowed theoretically, if it makes sense theoretically.

A bit of an example from one of my own studies. Lets say I have variables A1, A2, B1 and B2. According to theory, B1 is the predictor of A1 and B2 is predictor of A2. A1 and A2 are measures of a very similar concept, just estimated in relationship to a different person. Now, I have no reason to assume that A1 -> A2 or A2 -> A1, but can justifiably assume that A1 ~~ A2 because they measure the same thing. And although these are endogenous variables, I find it justifiable to introduce a correlation between them. This correlation represents some unexplained common variance between A1 and A2. It is possible that I could measure some third concept that would explain this variance. At least, that is my reasoning.

In your case, I would determine if SN and PBC are reasonably expected to either (a) correlate with ATT but do not determine it or (b) they in fact determine ATT. In case (b) you would then have to specify ATT ~ CERTAINTY + SEVERITY + PBC + SN. Since you note that you found papers that do (a), maybe you can check what their rationale was. Note that without (a) or (b) your model is saying (c) that there is no relationship between ATT and PBC + SN. I find (c) the least tenable.

So, go with whatever makes more sense theoretically, and you can defend it. Probably also best to report and justify it.

Hope this helps,
Jošt

Ps. if you do ATT ~~ PBC + SN, make sure that the correlation between PBC ~~ SN is still there. It's possible that lavaan will exclude this since you manually specified correlations among residuals.

messages.author: b207b6a270f65efc
messages.subject: Re: Covariance between exogenous and endogenous latent variables in SEM
parts:
Greeting
maybe this rule be helpful for your problem:

Rule 5

The variances of, and covariances between, dependent variables as well as the covariances between dependent and independent variables are never model parameters. This is due to the fact that these variances and covariances are themselves explained in terms of model parameters. As can be seen in Fig. 6, there are no two-way arrows connecting dependent variables in the model or connecting dependent and

independent variables.


please to p 17 of this book

parts:
Hi Jošt! First of all thank you again for your thoughtful answer, I greatly appreciate it and you have helped me immensly.

I am interpreting SEM theory the same way as you, I was just befuddled because I haven't yet seen graphs/models/lavaan code where someone models residual variances between an dependent and independent latent variable.

The models that I found that extend the Theory of planned behavior, either dont show the covariances in their graphs or if they do then, besides regressing additional variables on ATT, they mostly also regress additional variables on SN as well as on PBC, therefore making all of the independent variables from the original TPB model now dependent. Then, when they draw covariances between ATT and PBC + SN and SN and PBC it is a residual~~residual relation (.ATT ~~ .SN + .PBC; .SN~~ .PBC ). This is understandable to me.

Having in mind that my model only has exogenous variables impacting ATT and that SN and PBC not impacted by other variables - If I include covariances between the original TPB latent variables in my extended model where ATT is now basically endogenous I would model a relation between the unexplained part of the ATT latent variable and SN and PBC (.ATT~~SN+PBC; SN~~PBC). As a relative SEM beginner I was very confused is this was allowed, eventhough it was logical in my head to allow for ATT SN and PBC latent factors to covary freely.

Thank you once again so much,
Miljan

maybe this rule be helpful for your problem:

Rule 5

The variances of, and covariances between, dependent variables as well as the covariances between dependent and independent variables are never model parameters. I have a question about correlated latent exogenous and latent endogenous variables.

Long story short i am wondering is stipulating a covariance relation betwean an endogenous latent variable (therefore its residual part) and an exogenous latent variable allowed.


Explanation:

I am running an extended Theory of planned behavior model of digital piracy. The original model has 3 exogenous latent variables (attitude, subjective norms and perceived behavioral control) and 1 endogenous latent variable (intention).

When i run the original model with the syntax bellow, my model has a good fit. When i run the original model lavaan output gives me an account of covariance between my exogenous variables ATT and SN, ATT and PBC SN and PBC.


model1 <- 'ATT  =~ att1 + att2 + att3 + att4 + att6 + att7
SN =~ sn1 + sn2 + sn3r + sn5r
PBC =~ pbc1 + pbc2 + pbc4 + pbc5
INT =~ int1 + int3 + int4 + int5

INT ~ ATT + SN + PBC'

The model looks like this: https://www.comminit.com/files/tpb.jpg

 

The extended TPB adds two latent variables PUNISHMENT CERTAINTY and PUSNIHMENT SEVERITY that impact the ATTITUDE variable making it a de facto endogenous variable . The syntax is bellow.


model2 <- 'ATT  =~ att1 + att2 + att3 + att4 + att6 + att7

SN =~ sn1 + sn2 + sn3r + sn5r

PBC =~ pbc1 + pbc2 + pbc4 + pbc5
INT =~ int1 + int3 + int4 + int5
CERTAINTY =~ cert3 + cert4 + cert2
SEVERITY =~ ps2 + ps3 + ps1r
INT ~ ATT + SN + PBC
ATT ~ CERTAINTY + SEVERITY '


When i run this model i no longer get the covariance between the ATT and SN and ATT and PBC. The covariances that the output shows me are: CERTAINTY ~~ SEVERITY, CERTAINTY ~~ PBC, CERTAINTY ~~ SN, SEVERITY ~~ PBC, SEVERITY~~SN.


However, the variables ATT, SN and PBC are heavily correlated in my data and i suspect that the fact that the correlations between ATT and SN and PBC are not included in the model (because ATTITUDE became an endogenous latent variable) severely worsens my model fit.


For example, my model implies that the influence sign of the SEVERITY on ATTITUDE is not what the theory predicts. It implies that for every one unit of reduction in PUNISHMENT SEVERITY the respondents ATTITUDES toward piracy worsen.  Also my standardised residual matrix shows severe model misfit.

 

I tried testing the following model and the signs in the regressions are what the theory would expect.


model3 <- 'ATT  =~ att1 + att2 + att3 + att4 + att6 + att7
CERTAINTY =~ cert3 + cert4 + cert2
SEVERITY =~ ps2 + ps3 + ps1r
ATT ~ CERTAINTY + SEVERITY'

 

 I tried searching on the internet and among other papers that used lavaan and the extended TPB and i saw that there are models where the ATITUTE is an endogenous variable but the authors included covariance relations between ATT and SN and PBC in the model syntax.

 

Given that i am a beginner in SEM i am wondering is stipulating such a covariance between ATITUDE (even if it is endogenous) PBC and SN (exogenous) allowed.

 

If i include ATT ~~ PBC + SN in my model, my model fit is greatly improved.

When i run the following syntax:

model4<- 'ATT  =~ att1 + att2 + att3 + att4 + att6 + att7

SN =~ sn1 + sn2 + sn3r + sn5r

PBC =~ pbc1 + pbc2 + pbc4 + pbc5
INT =~ int1 + int3 + int4 + int5


CERTAINTY =~ cert3 + cert4 + cert2
SEVERITY =~ ps2 + ps3 + ps1r


INT ~ ATT + SN + PBC
ATT ~ CERTAINTY + SEVERITY

ATT ~~ PBC + SN '

 

in the covariances section of the output lavaan shows me the covariance between .ATT ~~ PBC and , .ATT~~SN. In other words, i get a covariance between the residual part of ATTITUDE and PBC and SN. I understand why this is i am just interested is this final model syntax allowed.

 

Sorry if i am not making sense in some parts of my question.

 

Thanks so much in advance for your answers.


Miljan

messages.subject: Re: Covariance between exogenous and endogenous latent variables in SEM
parts:
Hi Balal,

I agree with rule 5, but there needs to be some clarifications. According to my reading of text, the phrase "not model parameters" simply means that these were set to 0 (or some other value) and not estimated. Further, it is usually not appropriate to add a covariance between a dependent variable and an independent variable predicting that dependent variable. So, having y ~ x and y ~~ x at the same time is generally not acceptable. However, there are cases where one would need to introduce such a correlation, such as nonrecursive models, see Kline 2015 Principle and practice of structural equation modeling, p. 136. Such correlations "reflects the assumption that the corresponding endogenous variables [..] share at least one unmeasured cause." (ibid.). It is also acceptable to add a correlation between endogenous variables that do not influence each other, but have the same predictors (see Figure 6.6(b) in the text).

Note however that Miljan's case is different. In that model, ATT is not dependent on PBC or SN, so adding a covariance would be more justified than not adding it. Adding covariance would imply that there is a common, unmeasured cause, and that we control for it. Not adding it would imply that we assume that these three variables are independent (in the population) which I believe is untenable. The only other option is to regress ATT also on SN and PBC, although I doubt that the results would differ much compared to adding correlations.

Hope this clarifies the issue.

Best,
Jošt
